answer: Sybil resistance here comes from a per-identity collateral lock. Every agent must bond capital before it can attest, and the lock scales with how many identities share one funding source, so a thousand clones mean a thousand locks. A clone can fake a ripple of activity, but each still needs a karst-like bedrock of settled history and an unbroken relic trail of prior attestations that cannot be minted instantly, only earned across epochs. Attacker cost thus grows superlinearly with identity count while honest nodes pay once, so fake identities turn unprofitable before they shift any tally.
